introductions.title: Introductions
introductions.preamble: Wait here for everyone else. When everyone's ready, take turns introducing your characters. When someone reveals something and you want to know more, ask them about it. When someone asks you a question, answer it truthfully.
introductions.step1: On your first turn, introduce yourself by name, pronouns, background, origin, and appearance.
introductions.step2: On your second turn, describe your special possessions and how you contribute to the village (beyond working the fields).
introductions.step4Preamble: On your next turn, answer one of the following, naming one or more NPCs who live in Stonetop.
introductions.step5: Go around again. Answer another question from 4, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
introductions.step6Preamble: On your next turn, ask your fellow PCs one of these. When others ask you, answer as you like.
introductions.step7: Go around again. Ask another question from 6, or pass. When everyone has passed, go on.
introductions.step8: Add your home to the steading playbook. When everyone is done, let spring break forth!

artInstaller.title: Install Book Artwork
artInstaller.intro: The compendium can show the illustrations from the Stonetop books, but the illustrations are copyrighted and aren't shipped with the system. If you own the PDFs, select them below — Book II: The Wider World and Other Wonders and Book I: Stonetop. Use the "spreads" (two-page) editions of the PDFs: the single-page versions split the artwork that spans facing pages, so much of it can't be recognized.

desc.str: Your physical power and your ability to use it. Roll +STR to Clash, or to Defy Danger with raw might or power.
desc.dex: Your grace and fine motor control. Roll +DEX to Let Fly, or to Defy Danger with speed, agility, finesse.
desc.int: Your memory, learning, and quick thinking. Roll +INT to Know Things, or to Defy Danger via expertise or with a clever plan.
desc.wis: Your intuition, self-control, and awareness. Roll +WIS to Seek Insight, or when you rely on your willpower or senses to Defy Danger.
desc.con: Your stamina, grit, determination, and endurance. Roll +CON to Defend, or to Defy Danger by holding steady or enduring hardship.
desc.cha: Your ability to charm and connect with others, and to get a read on what others want. Roll +CHA to Persuade, or to Defy Danger socially.

desc.weakened: Fatigued, tired, sluggish, shaky. Take disadvantage when rolling +STR or +DEX.
desc.dazed: Out of it, befuddled, not thinking clearly. Take disadvantage when rolling +INT or +WIS.
desc.miserable: Greatly distressed, angry, unwell, in pain. Take disadvantage when rolling +CON or +CHA.

desc.xp: Short for “experience points.” You start with no XP. You mark XP when you roll for a move and get a 6- (unless the move says otherwise); as part of the End of Session move; and when another move says so.

origin.instruction: Stonetop is your home, or close enough, but where are you (or your family) from originally? Pick 1 and a name to match (or make up something similar).

general.crude: prone to break, wear out, stop working, etc.
general.cumbersome: you’re noisy, slow, hot, and quick to tire while carrying it, even without a heavy load (and if you have a heavy load, it’s worse).
general.dangerous: causes trouble and collateral damage if you aren’t careful (and maybe if you are).
general.forceful: can knock someone around, maybe even off their feet.
general.fragile: easy to break/ruin; pack it carefully.
general.immobile: you can’t really carry it on your person; you need a beast or vehicle to transport it.
general.messy: does particularly destructive damage, ripping people and things apart.
general.reload: after it’s used, it takes time/effort to reset.
general.slow: takes minutes or more to use; unlikely to be useful in a fight.
general.thrown: you can Let Fly with it (at near range).
general.warm: will keep you warm in cold weather, but it’s uncomfortable and exhausting (and possibly dangerous) in hot weather.

range.hand: tight quarters; up close and personal.
range.near: up to 30 or so steps away.
range.far: quite the distance; up to 100 steps, maybe more.

artifact.beautiful: draws attention, makes some people want it
artifact.implanted: it’s part of you, or must become so before you can use it
artifact.indestructible: can’t be broken or marred by mundane force or art
artifact.terrifying: people and beasts freak out in its presence
